sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

Heard Mr. B.C. Ghadei, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. B. Mohanty,
learned Addl. Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties.

3. The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking direction to the opposite parties not to evict him from the schedule plot situated over Khata No.300, Plot No.1303, Kisam-Gramya Jungle, measuring area Ac.0.05 dec., Mouza-Khaira, P.S./Tahasil- Boden in the district of Nuapada, and further seeks direction to the opposite parties to pay compensation to him in case of his eviction from the above mentioned plot like other land oustee of the said locality.
4.

Mr. B.C. Ghadei, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner fairly contended that the petitioner was in unauthorized occupation of the government land, but, due to acquisition of said land he was evicted and, as such, he was staying there by constructing a house.
Therefore, at best the petitioner can be compensated for the construction of his house from where he was evicted.

Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties contended that the petitioner was in unauthorized occupation of a government land, for which he has been duly compensated and, as such, the petitioner has been allotted another land and also provided a house under the Government scheme.
Therefore, question of any compensation for demolition of his house for unauthorized occupation of government land, does not arise.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that the petitioner has been provided with a land, as per sl.no.(b) of para-03, i.e., a house under PMAY 2017-18, which has already been constructed and possessed by him/his family.

1 constructed under PMAY 2017-18 is another house of the petitioner other than the house on the alignment of the BEW.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, notice in Form "Kha" was issued on 12.12.2019 to vacate the land within 30 days and due procedure, as prescribed under OPLE Act, 1972 and Rules, 1985, has been followed for eviction of the government land from unauthorized occupation of the petitioner.

As regards payment of compensation on eviction from the encroached government land (structure etc.), since the petitioner has been provided with alternative accommodation by providing land and house, he has been duly compensated.
7. In the above view of the matter, the writ petition merits no consideration and the same is hereby dismissed.
